title: Il passato prossimo con avere
summary: Building the passato prossimo with avere: regular participles -ato/-uto/-ito

blocks.title: Two pieces, one new tense
blocks.body: The **passato prossimo** talks about things that happened recently or are finished. It's built from two pieces: **avere** (in the present) + the **past participle**: *ho parlato* (I spoke / I've spoken). Most transitive verbs use avere — you'll see it everywhere.

blocks.title: -ato, -uto, -ito
blocks.body: The regular participle ending depends on the conjugation class: **-are → -ato**, **-ere → -uto**, **-ire → -ito**. Easy to build once you know the pattern.

blocks.prompt: What's the passato prossimo of *mangiare* (to eat) — 'I ate'?
blocks.explain: *Mangiare* is an -are verb: participle *mangiato*, with avere — *ho mangiato*.

blocks.prompt: Which ending goes with -ere verbs like *avere*?

pairs.left: *Parlo italiano ogni giorno.* — I speak Italian every day (habit, present)
pairs.right: *Ho parlato italiano ieri.* — I spoke Italian yesterday (finished event)
pairs.note: Same verb, different job — presente for habits, passato prossimo for finished events.

blocks.prompt: Type the passato prossimo of *lavorare* (to work) — 'I worked'.
Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.scene: At the bar, Marco asks You about the day

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.en: So, what did you do today?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ho lavorato tutta la mattina, poi ho pranzato con Giulia.
lines.en: I worked all morning, then I had lunch with Giulia.
lines.spotlight: Two avere-verbs back to back: ho lavorato, ho pranzato.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.en: You talked about work, I imagine.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Un po', sì. Ho anche ascoltato un po' di musica al bar.
lines.en: A little, yes. I also listened to some music at the bar.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Bello! Io invece ho dormito fino a tardi.
lines.en: Nice! I, on the other hand, slept in late.

blocks.prompt: Write 2-3 sentences about what you did today, using ho + a participle (-ato/-uto/-ito).
